tasks.short: Turn Finance Director budget instructions into clear planning guidance for Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo.

today.trigger: The Finance Director issues annual budget instructions or changes assumptions, spending limits or forecast requirements.
steps: Read the instructions and compare them with existing budget guidance and templates.
Check implications for site budgets, payroll assumptions, agency labour and spending approvals.
Resolve unclear instructions with the Finance Director, Controller and relevant HR colleagues.
Update the guidance and Excel templates, obtain approval and explain changes to budget holders.
drudgery: Comparing document versions and repeating changes across templates.
Answering the same interpretation questions from different sites.
Checking whether every template uses the approved assumptions.
today.time_sinks: Likely bottlenecks are conflicting instructions, scattered approvals and repeated explanations. The workflow is inferred from the company context; current handling time has not been measured.

lenses.faster: Document comparison, the first guidance draft and template consistency checks disappear from my manual work. For an illustrative two-hour update, I retain 20 minutes checking sources, 30 resolving interpretations, 20 aligning with approvers and 14 finalising guidance: 84 minutes including review.
lenses.autonomous: A new approved directive starts document comparison and preparation of a cited change list, draft guidance and template checks. I lead interpretation, and the Finance Director approves policy changes before publication.
lenses.ambitious: New service to site budget holders: a monthly briefing showing exactly how changed assumptions affect each site's next forecast. Demand would probably grow if preparation became cheaper, especially during wage or agency-rate changes.
lenses.joy: I would drop repetitive document comparison and repeated explanations. I would spend more time making instructions workable with site managers before the forecast cycle starts.
lenses.options: Compare a common spending limit, site-specific limits and an exception route against actual operating needs. These alternatives change who can authorise spending and how quickly sites can respond.
lenses.altitude: My week shifts toward resolving conflicting assumptions and testing whether guidance produces comparable site forecasts. With delegated authority, I could settle routine interpretation questions within approved limits; the role becomes more expert in finance governance.
reach: Absorb the Controller's task of maintaining budget guidance and checking template compliance; learn the approval matrix, accounting policies and control documentation.

tasks.human_edge: I recognise when a seemingly clear directive conflicts with operating reality, CAO assumptions or an earlier management commitment, and negotiate an interpretation people will follow.
tasks.pattern_why: copilot: interpretation and agreement remain the core work. Document comparison and drafting support the analyst within a predictable review process; an autonomous agent adds little.

in_practice.trigger: The Finance Director places a new approved directive in the designated SharePoint folder.
steps: Retrieve the directive, current guidance, approval matrix and affected templates with their version dates.
Prepare a source-linked comparison and flag ambiguous or contradictory instructions.
Draft guidance, worked site examples and proposed template changes.
Have the analyst resolve interpretation questions and check payroll assumptions with HR where necessary.
Obtain Finance Director approval, publish the guidance and record the version used for the forecast.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst checks every policy interpretation; the Finance Director approves changes to spending authority, planning policy or mandatory assumptions.
systems: Company-approved enterprise AI workspace, subject to selection and configuration
data_needed: Approved directives and their effective dates
Approved CAO, employer-cost and agency-rate planning assumptions
in_practice.logs_to: A restricted SharePoint change register containing source versions, proposed changes, reviewer decisions and publication approval.

evidence.claim: Source comparison and drafting can support budget-policy interpretation, but local authority and judgement remain with management. The time saving is an unmeasured pilot estimate.
Power BI Copilot can summarise reports and answer questions, but requires prepared data and qualifying capacity; the cited documentation says non-English use is not officially supported.

risks: A draft can silently turn an ambiguous instruction into an unauthorised policy decision.
Old CAO assumptions or inconsistent effective dates can distort labour budgets across sites.
Workforce policy changes may require HR review and applicable works council advice or consent; budget guidance alone does not authorise them.
Sensitive planning material could be exposed through an unapproved AI workspace.
research_questions: How often do instructions conflict, and how much analyst time goes into interpretation versus document editing?
Can every planning assumption be traced to an approved source, owner and effective date?
Will the Finance Director delegate routine interpretations within explicit limits?
Does a pilot reduce total handling time after corrections, approval and budget-holder questions are included?

tasks.short: Compare warehouse investments, operating proposals and financing choices so management can decide what pays.

today.trigger: A site manager requests funding, proposes an operating change or asks whether to buy, lease or defer an investment.
steps: Clarify the proposal, alternatives, decision deadline and expected operating benefits.
Collect historical costs, supplier quotations, labour assumptions and financing terms.
Build an Excel comparison of cash flows, payback, net present value and sensitivities.
Challenge assumptions with the requester, Controller and relevant operational specialists.
Prepare a recommendation and present the trade-offs to the Finance Director or authorised investment approver.
drudgery: Transcribing quotations and checking units, dates and financing terms.
Reformatting sensitivity tables and decision papers.
today.time_sinks: Reconciling quoted costs with ledger history and obtaining credible benefit assumptions probably dominate. Neither the proposed workflow nor its handling-time baseline has been observed.

lenses.faster: Reusable calculations, quotation extraction and automatic scenario tables remove most model assembly and formatting. For an illustrative four-hour case, I retain 30 minutes validating inputs, 45 challenging scenarios, 30 discussing trade-offs and 15 finalising the recommendation: two hours including review.
lenses.autonomous: A complete investment-request pack starts extraction into a standard input sheet and calculation of approved comparison measures. I check extracted terms, choose credible alternatives and approve the recommendation before it reaches the investment approver.
lenses.ambitious: New service to site managers: compare purchase, lease and staged deployment before they commit to a preferred equipment specification. Demand would probably grow as smaller proposals become affordable to assess.
lenses.joy: I would stop rebuilding cash-flow schedules and copying quotation details. I would spend more time checking whether promised capacity, safety and labour benefits are achievable.
lenses.options: Compare buy, lease, repair and defer under different demand, utilisation and residual-value assumptions. A staged purchase may beat the highest headline return when demand is uncertain or cash is constrained.
lenses.altitude: My week shifts toward investment challenge and follow-up on realised benefits. I could gain delegated authority to return incomplete cases and certify that comparisons meet agreed standards; capital allocation remains with authorised management, while my modelling expertise deepens.
reach: Absorb the Controller's task of preparing initial investment appraisals; learn cash-flow conventions, tax and VAT treatment, lease accounting and bank covenant definitions.

tasks.human_edge: I judge whether benefits are operationally credible, expose double-counted savings and weigh service reliability, safety and strategic flexibility against the financial return.
tasks.pattern_why: copilot: fixed spreadsheet calculations handle the arithmetic, and a model can extract quotation terms and draft comparisons. The analyst must lead the choice of alternatives and the challenge of benefits.

in_practice.trigger: A requester submits an investment pack with quotations, expected benefits and an accountable business owner.
steps: Check completeness and extract quoted terms into a source-linked input sheet, flagging missing or conflicting details.
Have the analyst validate cash-flow timing, labour assumptions, financing terms and benefit ownership.
Run a controlled Excel model for the feasible alternatives using approved discount rates and accounting conventions.
Generate sensitivity tables and a draft decision paper that separates sourced facts from assumptions.
Review trade-offs with the requester and submit the analyst's recommendation for investment approval.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst approves model inputs and the recommendation; the authorised investment approver decides expenditure and financing commitments.
systems: Microsoft Excel with controlled calculation templates
AFAS Profit extracts and Power BI
Company-approved enterprise AI workspace, subject to selection and configuration
data_needed: Historical costs and approved operational workload data
CAO-based employer costs and agency rates
Discount rates, tax assumptions and relevant covenant terms
Benefit assumptions, owners and delivery dates
in_practice.logs_to: The SharePoint investment case file, retaining source documents, model version, assumptions, scenario outputs and signed approval.

evidence.claim: Standard cash-flow calculations and sensitivity tables can run deterministically; operational benefit estimates still require human challenge. The time saving is a pilot hypothesis.

OneStream describes current automation of data gathering, scenario mechanics and commentary, with capital allocation remaining a human decision; this does not establish the same capability in Noordhaven's installed systems.

risks: A precise model can conceal speculative benefits, double-counted labour savings or unrealistic utilisation.
Extraction mistakes in lease terms, indexation, VAT or payment timing can reverse the preferred option.
Named headcount assumptions introduce personal data; use aggregated staffing costs wherever possible under AVG/GDPR.
A financially attractive staffing or equipment proposal may require separate safety, HR or works council review before implementation.
research_questions: What proportion of recent cases fits a common model without changing its financial logic?
Can quotation extraction pass checks on payment timing, indexation, exclusions and financing terms?
Do completed investments have actual benefit data against which assumptions can be tested?
Does the pilot improve decision quality and total turnaround as well as spreadsheet preparation time?

tasks.short: Find practical ways for our sites to reduce costs and improve margins without damaging service.

today.trigger: A forecast misses its margin target, a site shows an unexplained cost increase or management asks for improvement ideas.
steps: Review site costs and margins against budget, prior periods and available workload measures.
Investigate apparent drivers using ledger details, payroll totals, agency invoices and manager explanations.
Develop improvement hypotheses and estimate their financial effect.
Discuss feasibility, service effects and implementation constraints with site managers.
Recommend a small set of actions and track whether the expected benefits appear.
drudgery: Repeating cost comparisons across three sites.
Manually reconciling agency costs and labour totals.
Refreshing opportunity lists whose assumptions are already outdated.
today.time_sinks: Separating price, volume, service mix and timing effects takes time, especially without linked operational data. The supplied stack does not establish that shipment, warehouse throughput or service-quality data is available.

lenses.faster: Scheduled comparisons and a source-linked shortlist remove repeated workbook refreshes and first-pass investigation. For an illustrative four-hour review, I retain 36 minutes validating drivers, 30 assessing ideas, 60 discussing feasibility and 30 designing follow-up: 156 minutes including review.
lenses.autonomous: After the nightly AFAS extract passes reconciliation, rules flag material cost movements and a model drafts possible explanations with evidence gaps. I choose what to investigate, and site management approves any operational experiment.
lenses.ambitious: More frequent decision: a weekly choice of which agency-labour cost issue deserves a site-level experiment, using workload and service measures as safeguards. Demand would probably grow if preparation became cheaper, provided operational data is available at that frequency.
lenses.joy: I would drop repetitive comparisons and chasing explanations for timing differences. I would spend more time with site teams testing changes and checking whether benefits survive in practice.
lenses.options: Compare tighter agency ordering, overtime changes and cross-training against demand and service scenarios. Showing their different costs, lead times and service risks can change which experiment management funds.
lenses.altitude: My week shifts from reporting adverse variances to running an evidence-based improvement pipeline with site managers. I could gain authority to prioritise financial investigations and validate benefit claims; the job becomes more expert in operational economics and causal analysis.
reach: Absorb the Controller's task of maintaining a cost-improvement benefits register; learn baseline design, attribution and controls against double-counting.

Absorb the People Analytics and HRIS Analyst's task of preparing aggregated labour-cost comparisons for financial investigations; learn workforce definitions, CAO cost drivers and privacy-safe aggregation.

tasks.human_edge: I distinguish a real opportunity from a misleading correlation and understand when a proposed saving would damage service, safety, workforce trust or a site's ability to handle peaks.
tasks.pattern_why: copilot: deterministic comparisons can surface signals and a model can suggest hypotheses, but choosing useful experiments requires local knowledge and discussion. Unpredictable investigation alone does not justify giving an agent decision authority.

in_practice.trigger: The nightly AFAS extract passes control checks and a scheduled site-cost review becomes due.
steps: Reconcile cost totals and align periods, site definitions and agency invoice timing.
Calculate material movements and unit costs only where compatible workload measures exist.
Draft a ranked investigation list with source references, alternative explanations and missing evidence.
Have the analyst and site manager select a feasible experiment and agree cost, service and safety measures.
Track results against the agreed baseline and submit validated benefits for Controller review.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst validates each opportunity; the site manager approves operational trials, with HR, safety specialists and the works council involved where the proposed change requires it.
systems: Company-approved enterprise AI workspace, subject to selection and configuration
data_needed: Reconciled site costs, budgets and forecast assumptions
Aggregated payroll, overtime and agency hours and rates
Approved workload measures by site and comparable period, if available
Service, quality and safety measures for proposed experiments
Operational context and records of previous improvement actions
in_practice.logs_to: A restricted SharePoint opportunity register recording source snapshots, hypotheses, rejected explanations, experiment approvals and verified benefits.

evidence.claim: Pigment's finance-executive survey reports benefits from AI in variance analysis and scenario planning, but its self-reported findings do not establish causal gains or Noordhaven-specific savings.
Power BI Copilot can support report summaries and questions, but Microsoft warns that inadequate model preparation can cause data misinterpretation.
Reliable unit-cost comparisons require compatible workload data and controls for service mix; the proposed time saving depends on data not confirmed in the supplied stack.

risks: Site differences in workload, customer mix or invoice timing can look like inefficiency.
Cost reductions may move work elsewhere or harm service and safety without producing a net benefit.
More automated opportunity reports can consume management attention without improving decisions.
Individual worker scoring or staffing decisions would change the privacy and potentially EU AI Act assessment; keep this workflow focused on aggregated financial investigation.
research_questions: Can finance costs be joined reliably to workload and service measures across all three sites?
Which apparent historical opportunities remain after controlling for volume, mix and invoice timing?
Will site managers run measurable trials and provide enough operational context to test the hypotheses?
Do validated benefits exceed investigation, implementation and ongoing reporting effort?

role.altitude: The analyst becomes a financial decision partner for the three sites, spending more time challenging forecast drivers, comparing investments and validating benefits. Delegated rights could cover routine budget interpretation, investment-case completeness and investigation priorities; spending and workforce decisions remain with their authorised owners.
reach: Controller: budget guidance maintenance, initial investment appraisals and benefits-register preparation, with accounting and control training.
People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: aggregated labour-cost comparisons for financial planning, with shared definitions and privacy training.
role.ceiling_note: These tasks total 268.4 hours per FTE annually. Applying the unmeasured savings estimates gives about 102 hours per FTE, or 203 hours across both analysts, before setup and maintenance; meetings, interpretation and operational validation limit further savings, and added service demand could consume the released time.
skills_to_grow: Controlled Excel models, Power Query and reproducible source-to-output workpapers
Power BI semantic modelling and financial data reconciliation
Operational cost drivers, forecast calibration and experiment design
Investment appraisal, financing terms and benefit validation
CAO labour-cost assumptions, works council processes and AVG/GDPR-aware analysis
Clear recommendations that distinguish evidence, assumptions and management choices
role.ambitious_version: Provide monthly rolling forecasts for Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo, with explicit workload, labour-rate and agency-use scenarios. Use the time released to challenge assumptions with site managers, compare feasible actions and check forecast accuracy and realised benefits, while keeping outputs tied to the reconciled close.
